chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Maysara, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he was in a furnished room, wearing a damp shirt and a dyed sheet, the effects of the dye showing on his shoulders. So I began looking at the room and looking at his appearance.
He said: 'O Hakam! What do you say about this?' I said: 'And what could I say while I see it upon you? Among us, only the reckless young man does this.'
He said to me: 'O Hakam! Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He brought forth for His servants and the wholesome things of provision?' [Quran 7:32]
And this is from what God has brought forth for His servants. As for this room you see, it is the ladies' chamber, and I am recently wed. My room is the one you know.

key_terms.الطَّيِّبَات: Wholesome/good things of provision — the lawful pleasures and comforts God has permitted
key_terms.الْمُرَهَّق: The reckless or dissolute young man — al-Hakam's implicit social critique of ostentation
key_terms.بَيْت مُنَجَّد: A furnished or decorated room, with soft furnishings and cushions — a marker of comfort and wealth
key_terms.زِينَة اللَّه: The adornments of God — referring to Quran 7:32, all things God has made lawful for His servants' enjoyment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about wearing dyed clothing and adorning one's home?
ai.summary: Al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba, a Kufan jurist and companion of Imam al-Baqir (AS), was surprised to find the Imam in a decorated room wearing freshly dyed garments. When al-Hakam expressed implicit disapproval by associating such dress with reckless youth, the Imam responded by citing Quran 7:32 — the rhetorical question 'Who has forbidden God's adornments?' — affirming the permissibility of fine garments and lawful pleasures. The Imam then clarified the context: the decorated room belonged to his wife as he had recently married, while his own room was one al-Hakam already knew to be simpler.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Mayassar, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was in a recently furbished room, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a dyed shirt and a dyed sheet, the effects of the dye being upon his shoulders. So he<sup>asws</sup> went on to look at the room and looking at its furnishings, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Hakam! What are you saying regarding this?’ So I said, ‘And what I was about to say, and I saw it upon you<sup>asws</sup>, and as for with us, so it is rather the worn-out youth who are doing it’.
So heasws said to me: ‘O Hakam! [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?
And this is from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Brought forth for His<sup>azwj</sup> servants.
So As for this room which you see, so it is the ladies chamber, and I<sup>asws</sup> am very close to the time of the wedding, and my<sup>asws</sup> room is the room which you know’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Maysarah from al- Hakam ibn ‘Utaybah who has said the following:

“I once visited abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in a well-furnished house. He (the Imam) was wearing a shirt which was not fully dry and a colored bed sheet which had left its color marks on his shoulder, and I was looking at the house and to him (the Imam).
He (the Imam) said, ‘O Hakam, what do you say about it?’ I replied, ’I was about to say something about it after seeing it on you. With us it is used only by the youthful ones.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘O Hakam, ‘Who has made unlawful the beautiful things that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has brought out for His servants and the very fine kinds of means of sustenance/ [7:31]

This is of the things that Allah has made to come out for His servants. This house which you see is the house of the woman and I am not far away from the time of the wedding, however, my house is that which you know/”
